focus: Root framework: REPO RULES.md trigger router and AGENTS.md against Ponytail's always-on model
noveltyJustification: One finding is fully new (the close-out contract never discloses a residual risk), two are partially new (accessibility at root scope, trigger-table coverage verification), and two reconfirm self-application and adapter alignment as adopted.
keyQuestions: Which Ponytail teachings improve the root REPO RULES.md and AGENTS.md framework, including the trigger-table load model?
answeredQuestions: Which Ponytail teachings improve the root REPO RULES.md and AGENTS.md framework, including the trigger-table load model?

ruledOut.approach: Add a compact never-cut list as a second root file
ruledOut.reason: The floors are deliberately distributed at their points of use; a consolidated copy would drift, which the precedence clause exists to avoid. The accessibility extension is one line in existing homes.

ruledOut.approach: Import Ponytail's persona framing at the root
ruledOut.reason: Rejected for the agent definitions in iteration 1; the root framework's enforcement tone makes the same argument.

ruledOut.approach: Replace the trigger router with an always-on compact file
ruledOut.reason: The router's known failure (a missed trigger) is already countered by Gate 5, load-before-action and the precedence ladder; a compact file would duplicate or drop detail.

label: The close-out contract never discloses a residual risk: Ponytail closes with what was skipped or not checked plus any risk the user must know, while the repo close-out lists what ran, what is inferred, what only the operator can verify and what is not done, and the word risk never appears in evidence-and-proof.md or communication-handoff.md. NEW for AGENTS.md Sec10 and evidence-and-proof.md Sec10.

Accessibility is absent from the root framework and the never-cut floor is split: Ponytail keeps one never-cut list including accessibility, while the root docs carry no list at all and the word accessibility appears in neither AGENTS.md nor REPO RULES.md. ALREADY-COVERED idea (round one), NEW target.

Ponytail's self-application clause is already implied by universal binding: the Four Laws and gates bind agent behavior without scoping to human users, and REPO RULES.md makes the router mandatory before the first write of the session. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

The adapter-alignment rule is carried by the precedence clause: Ponytail keeps copied rule text aligned with its always-on file, while the repo avoids root copies and bounds every rule file so AGENTS.md wins on disagreement. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

The trigger table mechanically covers every rule file: all 13 files under .skilled/repo-rules appear in the Load column, each rule's fires-when maps to a row, and the no-trigger fallback is explicit. VERIFIED, no gap.
